---
name: Backend Standards
description: Backend-first rules for TypeScript files in the SaaS foundation.
applyTo: "**/*.{ts,tsx}"
---

# Backend-first rules

1. Prefer Effect services, layers, and schemas for backend logic and contracts.
2. Avoid hiding backend behavior in UI components, and defer frontend expansion until backend workflows are usable end to end.
3. Keep runtime config, permission scopes, projection profiles, and field rules in shared packages. Runtime config declarations stay versioned in code, while effective no-redeploy state synchronizes bidirectionally with PostgreSQL-backed services. Code-side approval is the committed code change; database-side mutations require an authenticated user with the proper permissions.
4. Keep package entrypoints thin. `index.ts` files should re-export focused backend modules rather than hold large contract or manifest registries.
5. Prefer small adapters around Keycloak, Convex, PostgreSQL, and observability endpoints.
6. Add or update Jest tests when backend contracts or service behavior changes.
7. For first-party runtime paths, prefer `Schema.decodeUnknown` plus `Effect` composition over synchronous decoding and raw exceptions.
8. Derive shared exported types from Effect Schema instead of duplicating interface-only shapes when a schema already defines the contract.
9. Treat app routes and server functions as framework edges only: call shared Effects there, but keep backend behavior in shared packages.
10. Generated TanStack router files are allowed exceptions if they contain framework-generated `as any` casts; do not hand-edit them.
11. For static schema-backed constants, use `Schema.validateSync(schema)(value)` together with `satisfies` so invalid literals fail at compile time before runtime validation.
12. Reusable backend string vocabularies such as module ids, scopes, permissions, projection profiles, capabilities, config keys, feature-flag keys, shared host defaults, and platform adapter service names should be centralized in shared named constants plus schemas; runtime code and tests should import them instead of retyping raw strings. This includes `configSchemaType.*` for config declaration schema types (`boolean`, `string`, `number`, `stringOrNull`), `projectionProfile.*` for projection profile names, `configDefaultValue.*` for default-value sentinels such as `"inherit"`, and `platformAdapterServiceName.*` for adapter service-name literals.
13. Split large literal registries by domain before they turn into catch-all files; keep compatibility barrels re-export only.
14. When a shared package starts trending toward dozens of root-level files, create domain folders and move implementations there before the flat structure becomes the next monolith. Organize for growth from day one — create domain subfolders as soon as the first file in a concern area is added, never wait for accumulation to justify structure.
15. Follow the current shared-package folder taxonomies: contracts uses `access/`, `data/`, `module-registry/`, `runtime/`, and `domains/`; modules uses `access/`, `governance/`, `domains/`, and `persistence/`; platform adapters use `identity/`, `storage/`, `messaging/`, `observability/`, `features-billing/`, and `search/` with `packages/platform/src/adapters/index.ts` as the export barrel and `packages/platform/src/adapters/service-names.ts` as the shared adapter service-name vocabulary/helper file; config manifests use `access/`, `governance/`, `domains/`, `communication/`, and `data/` under `packages/config/src/manifests/`; module spec docs use the same five domain groups under `specs/02-modules/`; platform specs use `architecture/`, `access/`, `security/`, `runtime/`, and `domains/` under `specs/01-platform/`; ADRs use `architecture/`, `storage/`, `identity/`, `runtime/`, `communication/`, and `domains/` under `specs/03-adr/`; tests use `contracts/`, `modules/`, and `platform/` under `tests/`, with `tests/type-assertions.ts` as the root entrypoint and grouped compile-time assertions under `tests/type-assertions/` when needed.
16. Author module manifests through typed helpers so module-scoped config keys, feature flags, runtime-value keys, and owners are checked by the type system instead of plain strings. Every manifest must use `platformModuleId.*` for `moduleId` and `owner`, `defineModuleConfigKeys` / `defineModuleFeatureFlags` for typed key constants, `permissionScope.*` for `permissionScopes`, `platformScope.*` for `allowedScopes`, `configSchemaType.*` for the `schema` field, `projectionProfile.*` for `profile` fields, and `configDefaultValue.*` for sentinel default values like `"inherit"`. Key helpers accept **suffixes only** (e.g. `"session.idleTimeoutMinutes"`) and automatically prepend `platformModuleId.*` at runtime, so the module ID is never duplicated in key literals.
17. Module field paths must be declared through named `...Fields` constants via `defineModuleFields(...)`, then consumed through `defineProjectionDescriptors(...)` and `defineDataClassificationDeclarations(...)` instead of inline string arrays. Reuse the same field constants in closely related field-security declarations and tests when they describe the same fields.
18. Use `Schema.NonEmptyString` instead of `Schema.String` for environment variables, API keys, URLs, adapter configuration, and identifiers or payload fields where an empty string is never valid.
19. When a live runtime function decodes input with `Schema.decodeUnknown`, preserve the concrete parse error type (for example `ParseResult.ParseError`) instead of widening the error channel to `unknown`.
20. Represent recoverable backend failures through typed Effect errors (using `_tag` discriminants) rather than raw `throw new Error(...)` in first-party runtime code.
21. Reuse existing named exported schema types in consuming code instead of repeating `Schema.Schema.Type<typeof SomeSchema>` when a canonical alias already exists. For example, use `RequestContext` rather than `Schema.Schema.Type<typeof RequestContextSchema>` outside the alias definition itself.
22. Keep `unknown` limited to honest boundary cases such as raw undecoded input, external thrown values, arbitrary JSON payloads, or unavoidable generic-preserving casts. Decode or narrow it at the nearest boundary instead of carrying it deeper into first-party code.
23. In-memory caches and collections that grow with request volume must be bounded from day one. Set a `maxCacheSize`, evict expired entries first, then evict the oldest entry when the cache exceeds capacity.
24. Break-glass access must validate `expiresAt` against the current time. An expired break-glass context must be denied, not silently accepted.
25. Fields classified as `regulated-sensitive` must be redacted for any actor that is not `platform-operator` or `support-operator`. This check belongs in the field-security module, not in UI code. Fields classified as `secret` are always redacted. Anonymous actors may only see `public` fields.
26. Test fixtures and expectations must use shared constants (`platformModuleId.*`, `actorType.*`, `permissionScope.*`, `platformScope.*`, `dataClassification.*`, `projectionProfile.*`, `configSchemaType.*`). The only exception is raw strings used as decode inputs to explicitly test `Schema.decodeUnknown` boundary behavior.
27. Every security-sensitive path (break-glass expiry, regulated-sensitive redaction, tenant isolation, cache eviction) must have explicit test coverage.
28. Do not treat an adapter stub, placeholder snapshot, or in-memory scaffold as a completed capability. The owning module, persistence or audit ownership, and operator workflow must be explicit before the capability moves beyond scaffolded.
29. Governance-heavy flows such as config, approvals, audit, billing, entitlements, and compliance should use durable PostgreSQL-backed state as the source of truth. In-memory state is limited to bounded caches and local scaffolds.
30. Prefer finishing one vertical slice of adapter -> module/service -> operator workflow -> validation before adding more parallel integration stubs.
31. Platform adapter service names and healthcheck schemas should be sourced from `packages/platform/src/adapters/service-names.ts`, reusing `platformAdapterServiceName.*` and `createPlatformAdapterHealthcheckSchema(...)` instead of repeating raw service literals in adapter implementations or platform adapter tests.
32. Environment-derived runtime config must decode required env values at the boundary and fail fast when they are missing or empty. Do not hardcode localhost URLs, credentials, or fallback defaults inside first-party adapters or services.
33. When a backend change adds, removes, or repurposes runtime env values, update `.env.example` and the relevant operator docs in the same slice, and keep each required value clearly classified as seeded locally, generated during bootstrap, or external-provider supplied.
